added_lemmas.statement: Tan and Syrgkanis, Theorem 3.13, state under the assumptions of their Proposition 3.12 that discrepancy-selected TRAE has squared strong error \(O(\delta_n^{2\min\{\beta,1\}/(1+\min\{\beta,1\})})\) and squared weak error \(O(\delta_n^2)\); in particular, the strong-rate exponent saturates when \(\beta>1\).

source.locator: Theorem 3.13, Section 3.2, page 14; Proposition 3.12 immediately preceding it
source.verbatim_statement:
Theorem 3.13. Under the assumptions of Proposition 3.12, suppose that the regularization parameter \(\lambda_{\mathrm{dp}}\) is chosen by Algorithm 1 with a sufficiently large constant \(c_d>0\), then with probability at least \(1-\xi\),
\[
 \|\widehat h_{\lambda_{\mathrm{dp}}}-h_0\|^2
 \le O\!\left(\delta_n^{\frac{2\min\{\beta,1\}}{1+\min\{\beta,1\}}}\right),
 \qquad
 \|T(\widehat h_{\lambda_{\mathrm{dp}}}-h_0)\|^2
 \le O(\delta_n^2),
\]
where \(\delta_n\) is defined in (3.7).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Tan and Syrgkanis, arXiv:2603.01337v1, Theorem 3.13 in Section 3.2 (PDF page 14), with the assumption reference resolved to the immediately preceding Proposition 3.12.

statement_notes.justification: This proposition isolates the deterministic optimization supplied by the finite dyadic Tikhonov grid. For every candidate \(k_0\) satisfying \(0<s_{k_0,n}\le1\) and \(\texttt{ass:grid-coverage}\), the grid contains a level within a factor of two of the continuous bias--variance balance, which yields the stated factor-three bound.
statement_notes.gap: The calculation controls only the displayed grid functional and does not by itself control \(\|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2\). Zero benchmark defects are not premises of this proposition; they enter only in the later collapsed-path witness showing that the grid functional can vanish while the estimator's strong error remains positive.
statement_notes.consumer: Use this proposition only to simplify the deterministic oracle expression and read off its saturation exponent. Any estimator-level conclusion additionally needs training-critic coverage or another argument linking the trained path to the pseudo-true target.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem is an architecture-level diagnostic for the note-defined hybrid that trains each candidate with its own adversarial critic and then selects only among the resulting finite path using a common audit. The explicit two-atom construction proves that a training critic can omit a target direction even when the common audit detects that direction and the benchmark's target, audit, and learned-image defects all vanish.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem does not refute the published discrepancy-selected TRAE workflow of Tan and Syrgkanis or the published Regularized DeepIV workflow of Li et al. Their estimators, objectives, and assumptions are not the note-defined candidate-specific-training plus common-audit selector. In particular, Tan and Syrgkanis's Theorem 3.13, under the assumptions of their Proposition 3.12, remains the published TRAE saturation comparator.
statement_notes.consumer: Use the theorem to rule out uniform oracle inequalities for this exact path-restricted hybrid unless the training stage gains a condition that controls the training-coverage defect or is allowed to refit with the audit coordinates. Do not export the counterexample as a negative claim about published TRAE or Regularized DeepIV procedures.
